title: Peach Melba
description: Vanilla-poached peaches on vanilla ice cream under a raspberry purée. Escoffier created it in the 1890s for the Australian soprano Nellie Melba, and his own recipe runs to just two sentences.
notes:
2699—PÊCHES MELBA

Poach the peaches in vanilla-flavoured syrup. Dish them in a timbale upon a layer of vanilla ice-cream, and coat them with a raspberry purée.

A. Escoffier, *A Guide to Modern Cookery* (London: Heinemann, 1907), Chapter XX, Entremets (Sweets), recipe 2699, p. 778, Project Gutenberg eBook #71395. Checked against the page scan.

Adapted: quantities added for four servings, the peaches are peeled and halved after poaching, and the raspberry purée is sweetened and strained.
ingredients: 1 vanilla bean, split, or 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
1/4 cup (30 g) powdered sugar, or to taste
steps: Bring the water, sugar, and vanilla bean to a simmer in a saucepan just wide enough to hold the peaches, stirring until the sugar dissolves. (If using extract, add it after poaching.)
Add the whole peaches and poach at a bare simmer, turning once, until a knife slides in easily, 8 to 12 minutes depending on ripeness.
Let the peaches cool in the syrup, then slip off the skins, halve them, and remove the stones. Chill in the syrup for at least 1 hour.
Blend the raspberries with the powdered sugar and lemon juice, then press through a fine sieve to remove the seeds. Chill.
Spread a layer of ice cream in a chilled glass bowl or individual coupes. Arrange the peach halves on top and spoon the raspberry purée over to coat.
